headword: {耐震設計|たいしんせっけい}

definitions.explanation: The design of buildings and structures to withstand earthquake forces, a critical aspect of construction in earthquake-prone Japan.

examples.japanese: この{建物|たてもの}は{耐震設計|たいしんせっけい}だ。
{新|あたら}しいマンションは{最新|さいしん}の{耐震設計|たいしんせっけい}を{採用|さいよう}している。
examples.english: The new apartment building uses the latest seismic design.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}では{大|おお}きな{地震|じしん}が{多|おお}いため、{耐震設計|たいしんせっけい}の{基準|きじゅん}が{世界|せかい}でも{特|とく}に{厳|きび}しい。
examples.english: Because Japan experiences many large earthquakes, its seismic design standards are among the strictest in the world.

notes:
Compound of {耐震|たいしん} (earthquake resistance) and {設計|せっけい} (design; engineering). A fundamental concept in Japanese architecture and construction, especially after major earthquakes like the 1995 Hanshin-Awaji and 2011 Tohoku disasters prompted stricter building codes.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {耐震設計|たいしんせっけい}の{基準|きじゅん}: seismic design standards
- {耐震設計|たいしんせっけい}を{採用|さいよう}する: to adopt seismic design
- {耐震設計|たいしんせっけい}の{建物|たてもの}: earthquake-resistant building
- {最新|さいしん}の{耐震設計|たいしんせっけい}: state-of-the-art seismic design

RELATED TERMS:
- {耐震|たいしん}: earthquake resistance (the broader concept)
- {免震|めんしん}: seismic isolation (absorbs vibration rather than resisting it)
- {制震|せいしん}: vibration damping (reduces shaking with dampers)
- {耐震補強|たいしんほきょう}: seismic retrofitting
